rv.q: It bops along with mid-scale stakes, enjoyably enough for your holiday viewing, and I noticed it skillfully held the attention of the families who also attended the performance I saw.
See one play. See them both. But it is a serious disservice to yourself as a patron of the arts to not witness this thrilling new chapter for Chicago Shakespeare Theater.
Director Edward Hall has delivered a timeless, fast-paced, comic gem that will be just the tonic to warm the frosty air off Lake Michigan and the perfect complement for Hall’s new repertory company.

A Midsummer Night’s Dream is a straight-up joyride of mistaken identities, mischievous fairies, and “rude mechanicals” trying to put together a show-within-a-show that would make even Corky St. Clair from Waiting for Guffman weep at its ineptitude.

They brought Shakespeare's two timeless plays to life with outstanding performances infused with just the right amount of love and laughter, all wrapped in captivating energy that truly embodies the magic of live theater.
